The Steam app is has Steam Guard, Steam's 2FA, which makes the app worth having alone, and if that's all you need from it, it works, and works well.  However everything else about this app is slow and often broken, which is unacceptable given that Steam is the definitive place to purchase PC games.  For instance, load times for pages are abysmal. I have owned several phones, my current being the Galaxy A5 and previous was the LG G5, and the app runs poorly, which there is no excuse for on modern phones.  Sometimes things don't work, such as pages not loading at all, or confirmations (Used for confirming listing items on the market, trades, etc.) Which fails for seemingly no reason, and trying to go to another page such as the store page of a game will also not work some times (Notice a trend?)  Then the last point I have to make is more of something that I feel should be in the app but isn't, which is the ability to redeem codes from within the app. You can now redeem codes from a web browser, so the fact that you can't from within the official Steam app makes no sense.  TL;DR: Good if 2FA is all you need, basically terrible for anything else.

For the most part I really like the app. But the chat part of it needs to be fixed. Big time. Like many other people mentioned there has been a recent glitch that would require you to restart the app in order to temporarily fix the problem. The glitch would involve seeing the person type even when they're not typing. In other words, the "..." would be present one second then disappear the next. Rinse and repeat. I also would have other problems with the chat as well. Everytime I close the app, I would appear offline to the other person and they wouldn't be able to reply back to my messages. This makes it inconvenient because a lot of the time when this happens I'm not near a home computer or anything to switch to when it comes down to it. Sometimes I don't receive notifications of messages.  Update (May 1st): One problem that has been fixed about this app was that flashing typing screen that I mentioned previously. And on top of that I have been able to remain online even when the app is not open. Which is an improvement in my opinion. But another problem has come about. As of yesterday, I haven't been getting messages from the person I am replying to. I doubt that it has anything to do with their connection but I would find myself seeing that they're typing and then they would suddenly stop typing. And it's not the simple circumstance that they just stopped typing but in all actuality they sent the message but I just didn't get it right away. I would have to back out of the app and then in order to receive the message and then reopen the app.  All things considered it seems like that when problems are fixed new problems arise. Which is to be expected but when it's happening at such a rate like this it really unnerves me and I think that the app needs a lot more maintenance than what valve has been giving it.

It's a slow app that essentially just loads a mobile website. The rest is also built in HTML5 so even on the newest phone it'll be jittery, unresponsive and the buttons and links are fiddly.  What it should be? A native app that gets listings and certain design elements (for a holiday sale, for example) from an API and renders it pixel-perfect, so you get a snappy, beautiful app. Of course chat and community stuff is nice but it needs a lot of polish and a much better mobile focus to make that a fun thing to check out on your coffee break or when traveling home from work. On top of that it should notify you about sales of wishlist items, it should incorporate the market and let you know when you've made a sale, and most of all it should support mobile games. That's a huge addition to Valve's business model, but right now Humble Bundle is filling that gap. You're missing some easy earnings there, with the tons of Indie games you already support but that keep finding their own way in the mobile space. Mobile devices are slowly but surely nibbling away at the underbelly of gaming, where mobile sales of simpler games see far more sales than their Mac/PC/Linux counterparts.

In my opinion, the application is too much desktop-alike, it doesn't look like the team tried to make an application that would benefit from Android's graphical elements (for example, instead of using the regular Android menu, when you press the menu button, a custom menu appears). Overall, I believe this makes the application too "heavy" for a mobile device; what we really need is a lightweight application, that uses as little battery as possible. Another issue is the data traffic. With the application minimized, the traffic was about 1 Mb for 12 hours (I used 3G Watchdog Pro for measuring); that means 50-60 Mb for a month. IMHO it's WAY too heavy... I suppose the application polls the Steam servers, instead of taking advantage of Android's notification system (C2DM). In the end, I suppose this will also impact the battery usage. Still, the application is in Beta stage, which means the development team could improve it a lot in the next months :)

I have a few complaints about this app. Firstly, it goes against the design paradigms set in place by Google. The menus are in strange places which may confuse people. The GUI tries too hard, and as a result looks busy and performs poorly. (There's also some cases of severe color banding in certain areas, when by all rights we should be seeing solid colors for cleanliness and consistency.)  The chat functions well enough but has quite a bit of measurable delay from PC to mobile, measuring in several seconds. The app does not support group chat when it really should. The chat also has a noticeable impact on my Galaxy S. The chat also ends up in a separate notification in the notifications pane, so more often than not Steam will have two individual icons when it really shouldn't.  My biggest complaint is that the back button is broken. Instead of exiting my screen and going up a level, it sequentially goes back through all of the pages you've visited. It's very frustrating to use.  I would also like to be able to view my game library, and perhaps the library of others.   This is a great concept that has been long overdue. Valve, you should be careful not to drop the ball on this one.
